newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Hoechst plans merge specialty unit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hoechst plans merge specialty unit.

text.p: German Hoechst AG, Europe's largest chemicals group, on Tuesday said it plans to merge some of its specialty chemicals businesses with Swiss group Clariant AG, in a bid to improve sluggish performance in those areas.

Hoechst told German bourse authorities it would introduce its specialty chemicals business, pigments and additives as well as other businesses into the new group, which is expected to post nine billion marks ($5.8 billion) in annual sales.

Hoechst would take a sizeable minority stake in Clariant, which will remain a Swiss share company, quoted on the Zurich stock exchange. A large portion of the new group's business would be run by a German subsidiary, Hoechst said.
Hoechst will contribute some 6.5 billion marks in annual sales to the new group with Clariant providing some 2.7 billion marks, Hoechst said in the statement.
The move is expected to deliver considerable savings to both Hoechst and Clariant totalling several hundreds of million Swiss francs, it added.

The German group, which for some time has said it planned to find a partner for its underperforming specialty chemicals businesses, said the step "reflects the difficult situation in these business areas, especially in Europe."
"The broad product portfolio and the larger geographical presence will open up new growth opportunities," Hoechst said.

The markets cheered Hoechst's decision, sending shares up 2.3 percent to 70.50 marks when shares resumed trading following a brief suspension ordered by German bourse authorities. Clariant shares were also suspended from trade.
Clariant, which was spun off from Swiss drugs giant Sandoz AG in 1995, said it would make a statement this afternoon.
Analysts welcomed the deal, saying Hoechst had taken a bold step in revamping a sector that some analysts believed had been mismanaged for some time.
"This is certainly good news for each of the companies," said Tony Cox, analyst at Kleinwort Benson in London.
He added the move might further improve shareholder value for Hoechst as the group would effectively receive a share market quotation for certain businesses.

Hoechst, one of Germany's most vocal supporters of the concept of shareholder value, in November announced plans to make itself into a strategic management holding company turning its businesses into separate legal entities and seeking bourse listings for some of these groups.
The merger will result in a larger product portfolio as well as an improved geographical presence and new growth opportunities.
Hoechst's supervisory board has not yet approved the decision, but a company spokeswoman said a decision was expected this afternoon. Clariant's supervisory board had already approved the merger.
Clariant employs 8,700 in this sector while Hoechst employs 23,000 in the sector worldwide. Neither company has commented on potential job losses. ($1=1.5541 Mark)
